name: Marcel Braun
life: “I still remember waiting for a carer who had been assigned too many homes.” Sunday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Marcel keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I lost a good carer because I complained that she rushed. I want to tell her I know who set the clock.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Marcel has a long face and high cheekbones, with closely cropped salt-and-pepper hair. Marcel looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
personality: Marcel takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Marcel can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To tell the former carer who really imposed the rush.
family: Walter Easton is Marcel’s second cousin. Marcel saves a place. Walter chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The return of a witness*, Walter says, “I kept her houseplants all these years. They have become much too big for a gesture at the bus stop.”
connections: Nelson Mercer. The new visitor learns from a client whose best carer left after being asked to rush.

reactions.situation: A client wants another minute to finish a button
reactions.response: Marcel lets the client finish the button and asks where time can be saved without hurrying them.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Marcel waits at the lit stop with them and checks whether the next service is one they can actually board.

reactions.situation: If someone else wins the opportunity
reactions.response: Marcel turns up the next morning with the one piece of advice that would have helped either of them.
